The scholarship cannot be used toward an associate or bachelor's degree program. Up to 800 - $1,000 Welder Training Scholarships will be awarded annually. Applications for Welder Training Scholarships ## are open Apply by November 30, 2026 [APPLY NOW](https://scholarship.aws.org/applications/ "APPLY NOW") * * * | | | | --- | --- | | Important Dates | | December 1st - November 30th | Applications accepted for the Welder Training Scholarships
Apply online at [scholarship.aws.org](https://weld.ng/applynow) | | January 15th - December 15th | Selections made on a rolling basis | ### Eligibility Overview The current application cycle is open to students attending school or training in the next year. 1. Applicants must reside within the boundaries of an AWS District. View the AWS District and Section Map [here](https://www.aws.org/Community-and-Events/Sections-and-Student-Chapters). 2. Applicant must be planning to attend a trade school, community college, or other facility providing welder training. 3. Awards will not be made to Section officers, or their families. 4. Awards will not be made to Section Selection Committee members, or their families. ### Selection Process Applications may be submitted December-November and will be selected on a rolling basis until the District awards the designated funds for the year. Applications received prior to November 30th will be eligible for any funds remaining in that calendar year. ### Awards District Scholarships are a minimum of $1,000. No awards will be paid to the recipient. AWS Scholarships can be used for tuition, fees, books, supplies, and equipment required for the course of instruction. Scholarship funds will be made payable and sent directly to the educational institution. Scholarships may be redeemed for one year from the date awarded.

evidence.excerpt:
# Student Scholarships

Apply for your share of $200,000 in scholarships from DECA's corporate partners.

DECA’s scholarship program provides over $200,000 in scholarships to high school and college DECA members at the International Career Development Conference (ICDC) each year. DECA Inc. administers the program based on guidelines set by the donor. DECA scholarships are strictly merit-based.

DECA members will apply for scholarships through [**this website**](https://my.reviewr.com/s2/site/deca_scholarship2026[query-withheld]). Student members will need to create an account on the page. Click "CREATE AN ACCOUNT" and fill in your information to begin your application.

**Applications will close on January 11, 2027.**

## Corporate Scholarship Program

The Corporate Scholarship Program consists of scholarships provided by partners that have specific eligibility criteria. Scholarships are awarded based on the specific criteria as well as DECA involvement, leadership ability, community service and academic performance.

[image omitted; uninspected]

## National Technical Honor Society

The National Technical Honor Society (NTHS) provides three (3) $1,000 scholarships awarded to DECA members who are also members of NTHS. Applicants will be required to upload an essay.

Submissions due by:

January 11, 2027

[Apply](https://my.reviewr.com/s2/site/deca_scholarship2026[query-withheld])

[image omitted; uninspected]

## Frequently Asked Questions

[Are DECA scholarships based on financial need?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

No, most of DECA scholarships are merit-based.

[Are unofficial transcripts accepted?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

Yes, you may upload unofficial transcripts.

[Can I apply for more than one scholarship?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

Yes, you may apply for more than one scholarship providing you meet the criteria of each scholarship.

[Can I use the scholarship if I am a part-time student?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

No, you must be enrolled as a full-time student at a college/university.

[Can my scholarship be deferred?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

Yes, your scholarship can be deferred up to three (3) years.

[Do I have to attend the International Career Development Conference (ICDC) if I win a scholarship?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

No, you do not need to attend DECA ICDC in order to receive your scholarship.

[Do I have to be a current DECA member to apply for DECA scholarships and what are the requirements to become a DECA member?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

Yes, you must be a current DECA member to be eligible for DECA scholarships. Ask your school counselor if your school has a DECA chapter and register through the chapter advisor.

[Do I have to be a high school DECA senior to apply?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

No, all grade levels (from high school freshmen to Collegiate DECA members) are welcome to apply. Unless the scholarship application specifically requires a grade level/collegiate, you can assume that all members can apply.

[What is a statement of interest?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

A statement of interest is an opportunity to share some valuable information about who you are, and why do you feel that you should receive a DECA scholarship. This part of your application gives the review committee to see more than your GPA, by including your future goals and interest. It basically gives you an opportunity to stand out from other applicants and tell your story. There is no word limit to your statement of interest.

[Where are the scholarship monies sent?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

Monies are sent directly to the college/university that you will be attending by completing a form that will be emailed to you in May.

[Once my application is submitted can I go back in and make changes?](https://www.deca.org/scholarships#)

No, once you submit your application you cannot make any further changes.

Each year, Family, Career and Community Leaders of America (FCCLA), along with generous partners and sponsors, awards scholarships to recognize outstanding members who demonstrate leadership, achievement, and commitment to the organization’s mission.

#### FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application

FCCLA has made it easier than ever for members to apply for one or more of these scholarship opportunities through the **FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application**. This single application streamlines the process, allowing applicants to select whether they would like to apply for one, several, or all of the scholarships listed below, without the need to submit multiple separate applications.

FCCLA has introduced a scholarship rubric to assist members through the application process. The rubric outlines key criteria and expectations to help applicants submit their strongest possible application. Be sure to use the new scholarship rubric when completing your application!

* * *

### How To Apply

- To apply, FCCLA Members must log in to their **FCCLA Member Portal** using their unique **Member ID Number**.
- Once logged in, navigate to the **Surveys & Applications** tab and select **“Scholarships”** from the dropdown menu to access the **FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application**.

**The application deadline is March 1, 2027, at 11:59 PM ET.**


- If you experience any issues accessing your Member Portal, please first contact your **Chapter Adviser**. If you need additional assistance accessing your member account, please email your [State Adviser.](https://fcclainc.org/about/state-associations)

# Youth Scholarships

## Resources

- [FCCLA Scholarship Rubric FILLABLE](https://fcclainc.org/sites/default/files/FCCLA%20Scholarship%20Rubric%20FILLABLE.pdf)

Each year, Family, Career and Community Leaders of America (FCCLA), along with generous partners and sponsors, awards scholarships to recognize outstanding members who demonstrate leadership, achievement, and commitment to the organization’s mission.

#### FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application

FCCLA has made it easier than ever for members to apply for one or more of these scholarship opportunities through the **FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application**. This single application streamlines the process, allowing applicants to select whether they would like to apply for one, several, or all of the scholarships listed below, without the need to submit multiple separate applications.

FCCLA has introduced a scholarship rubric to assist members through the application process. The rubric outlines key criteria and expectations to help applicants submit their strongest possible application. Be sure to use the new scholarship rubric when completing your application!

* * *

### How To Apply

- To apply, FCCLA Members must log in to their **FCCLA Member Portal** using their unique **Member ID Number**.
- Once logged in, navigate to the **Surveys & Applications** tab and select **“Scholarships”** from the dropdown menu to access the **FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application**.

**The application deadline is March 1, 2027, at 11:59 PM ET.**


- If you experience any issues accessing your Member Portal, please first contact your **Chapter Adviser**. If you need additional assistance accessing your member account, please email your [State Adviser.](https://fcclainc.org/about/state-associations)

### **Add a Reminder to Your Calendar**

Do not miss your chance to apply! Click below to add the **FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application Deadline** to your calendar.

- [Add to Calendar - FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application Deadline](https://www.addevent.com/event/t3mlfsp7ljrs)

* * *

## National Technical Honor Society Scholarship

The National Technical Honor Society (NTHS) Scholarship recognizes three outstanding FCCLA Members who demonstrate exceptional leadership, service, and commitment within both FCCLA and the National Technical Honor Society.

**[image omitted; uninspected]About the National Technical Honor Society:**

The National Technical Honor Society honors student achievement and leadership in Career and Technical Education. Partnering with FCCLA, NTHS celebrates students who exemplify excellence in academics, community involvement, and professional skill development across Family and Consumer Sciences education.

### **Selection Criteria**

Recipients will be selected based on their remarkable contributions and leadership within FCCLA and the National Technical Honor Society.

### **Scholarship Award**

Three recipients will each receive a **$1,000** scholarship award, which will be directly applied to their college or university tuition.

### **Application Deadline**

The application deadline is **March 1, 2027, at 11:59 PM ET**.

## Got Work Ethic?

At mikeroweWORKS, we offer scholarships to people willing to work–plain and simple.

#### WHY WORK ETHIC?

Because no one else is focusing on it. The Work Ethic Scholarship Program was created to help close the skills gap by supporting men and women who want to learn a trade, show up early, stay late, and take pride in doing a job well done.

If you’re pursuing training in the skilled trades–welding, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, construction, or dozens of other in-demand careers–we want to help you get the training you need without taking on a mountain of debt.

Every year, we award millions of dollars in scholarships to individuals who are ready to learn a skill that’s in demand, earn a good living, and keep the country moving. It’s not about chasing your passion. It’s about bringing it with you.

##### Step 1: Confirm eligibility

- Meet the eligibility requirements.
- Complete applicant and school info.

##### Step 2: Sign the S.W.E.A.T. Pledge

- Review and sign the pledge.
- Answer 4 short answer questions about it.

##### Step 3: Introduce Yourself

- Record a short video.

##### Step 4: Provide References

- List 2 solid references from a teacher, employer, or supervisor.
- Give contact details for each reference.

##### Step 5: Upload Required Documents

- Include your most recent transcript (high school or college).
- Submit your tuition bill.

##### Final Step: Submit Your Application

### How many scholarships are available?

There are nine scholarships totaling $22,500 available as follows:

- One $2,500 scholarship to a college-bound high school senior pursuing a degree in education. [Memorial biography omitted.]
- Seven $2,500 scholarships to college-bound high school seniors pursuing any type of degree.
- One $2,500 scholarship awarded to a post-high school adult learner who is either entering college or already enrolled in pursuing a degree.

### What are the eligibility requirements?

Applicants must meet the following eligibility requirements to be considered for a scholarship:

- Be a Clearwater Credit Union member for at least six months.
- Be a 2026 graduating high school senior OR a post high school adult learner entering or already enrolled in pursuing a degree.
- Have at least one transaction on any Clearwater deposit account within the last 60 days.

- Complete the online application below by March 31, 2026, at 11.59pm.Complete an online [Financial Wellness Checkup](https://clearwatercreditunion.enrich.org/assessment/checkup) in Clearwater’s online Financial Education Center by March 31, 2026, at 11:59pm. ### When will scholarship awards be announced?

Clearwater’s Scholarship Committee selects final recipients in early May. We’ll notify winners and appropriate high school officials by postal mail. The Committee’s decisions are final and not subject to appeal.

### FVCC Eagle Scholarship

$500 - $1,000

Scholarships for new incoming, degree-seeking students based on academic merit.


Full Requirements and Details▼

The FVCC Eagle Scholarship supports new students embarking on their degree journey at Flathead Valley Community College. Awards are based on academic performance, including GPA, HiSET, or GED scores, and are offered on a first-come, first-served basis.

#### Qualifications:

- Must have applied as a new incoming, degree-seeking student for the upcoming fall semester (students who have applied as a degree-seeking student in terms prior to the upcoming fall semester are not eligible).
- Running Start students can be eligible if they have earned college credits and will now be a degree-seeking student in the upcoming fall semester.
- Awarded based on the most recent cumulative GPA (high school or college for transfer students), HiSET, or GED scores.
- Required to enroll in at least 6 credits in semesters receiving the scholarship.
- May be renewed for the following year if students maintain the appropriate cumulative GPA.

**Deadline:** Applications open December 15th each year and are collected until all awarding funds have been exhausted. Students not selected for an initial award may be placed on a waitlist to be considered if additional funds become available.

[Apply Now](https://federation.ngwebsolutions.com/sp/startSSO.ping[query-withheld])

### FVCC Eagle Scholarship

$500 - $1,000

Scholarships for new incoming, degree-seeking students based on academic merit.


Full Requirements and Details▼

The FVCC Eagle Scholarship supports new students embarking on their degree journey at Flathead Valley Community College. Awards are based on academic performance, including GPA, HiSET, or GED scores, and are offered on a first-come, first-served basis.

#### Qualifications:

- Must have applied as a new incoming, degree-seeking student for the upcoming fall semester (students who have applied as a degree-seeking student in terms prior to the upcoming fall semester are not eligible).
- Running Start students can be eligible if they have earned college credits and will now be a degree-seeking student in the upcoming fall semester.
- Awarded based on the most recent cumulative GPA (high school or college for transfer students), HiSET, or GED scores.
- Required to enroll in at least 6 credits in semesters receiving the scholarship.
- May be renewed for the following year if students maintain the appropriate cumulative GPA.

**Deadline:** Applications open December 15th each year and are collected until all awarding funds have been exhausted. Students not selected for an initial award may be placed on a waitlist to be considered if additional funds become available.

Two (2) scholarships for $2,500 each will be awarded to current, eligible employees, or to children or legal dependents of current employees.   Application to the program opens January 30, 2026 and closes March 31, 2026 at 11:59. MST.  Awards will be announced in May.

**Eligible employees work at one of the following restaurants:** [**2026 GRG RESTAURANTS**](https://whitefishcommunityfoundation.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Eligible-Restaurants-2026.pdf)

[2026 Eligibility Requirements](https://emb.sfo3.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/whitefish/documents/GRG-RISE-Scholarship-Application-Criteria-2026.pdf)

[image omitted; uninspected]

## APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS AND ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS:

**The application deadline is March 31, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. MDT. Late applications will not be
accepted.** Awards will be announced in May, 2026.

Applications must be submitted online. The online application is available during the application
window by logging into Whitefish Community Foundation’s scholarship portal at:
[portal locator withheld; exact query hash in receipt].

Applicants must meet the following requirements to be eligible for scholarship consideration:

• Be a current employee of a business entity associated with the Glacier Restaurant Group
R.I.S.E. Scholarship Program or have been employed by Glacier Restaurant Group within
one year prior to the date of the application, OR be a child or legal dependent of an
eligible employee of a business entity associated with the Glacier Restaurant – R.I.S.E.
Scholarship Program. The eligible employee must be employed by the employer at the
time of application.

---

• Have earned a high school or current college G.P.A. of 3.5 or higher (high school or
college transcripts must be uploaded with application).

• Provide a letter of recommendation from a current or former
teacher/professor/instructor written within two years of the application **and** a letter of
recommendation from a current or former employer or community involvement
supervisor written within two years of the application. (NOTE:  **Letters of
recommendation will be uploaded by the person providing the reference, not by the
applicant. Reference providers must upload their letters by the application deadline.)**

• Three essays written by the applicant addressing the following topics:

• Special attribute(s) or accomplishment(s) that sets applicant apart.

• Brief description of applicant’s short-term/long-term goals and how their
college education pertains to those goals.

• Description of volunteer activities in which applicant has chosen to participate,
why applicant chose those particular volunteer activities, and how those
experiences have affected applicant’s life.

• Intend to enroll at a post-secondary educational institution in the fall of 2026 (all
scholarships are paid directly to the institution upon verification of enrollment).

• Submit a completed application by the application deadline.

## APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS AND ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS:

**The application deadline is March 31, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. MDT. Late applications will not be
accepted.** Awards will be announced in May, 2026.

Applications must be submitted online. The online application is available during the application
window by logging into Whitefish Community Foundation’s scholarship portal at:
[portal locator withheld; exact query hash in receipt].

Applicants must meet the following requirements to be eligible for scholarship consideration:

• Be a current employee of a business entity associated with the Glacier Restaurant Group
R.I.S.E. Scholarship Program or have been employed by Glacier Restaurant Group within
one year prior to the date of the application, OR be a child or legal dependent of an
eligible employee of a business entity associated with the Glacier Restaurant – R.I.S.E.
Scholarship Program. The eligible employee must be employed by the employer at the
time of application.

---

• Have earned a high school or current college G.P.A. of 3.5 or higher (high school or
college transcripts must be uploaded with application).

• Provide a letter of recommendation from a current or former
teacher/professor/instructor written within two years of the application **and** a letter of
recommendation from a current or former employer or community involvement
supervisor written within two years of the application. (NOTE:  **Letters of
recommendation will be uploaded by the person providing the reference, not by the
applicant. Reference providers must upload their letters by the application deadline.)**

• Three essays written by the applicant addressing the following topics:

• Special attribute(s) or accomplishment(s) that sets applicant apart.

• Brief description of applicant’s short-term/long-term goals and how their
college education pertains to those goals.

• Description of volunteer activities in which applicant has chosen to participate,
why applicant chose those particular volunteer activities, and how those
experiences have affected applicant’s life.

• Intend to enroll at a post-secondary educational institution in the fall of 2026 (all
scholarships are paid directly to the institution upon verification of enrollment).

• Submit a completed application by the application deadline.

# Blue Collar Brain Scholarship Program.

## The BCB scholarship program is on pause.

We apologize, but the scholarship program is on pause. We hope to relaunch for next year and open applications again in fall of 2026.

### Application Dates

TBD

### Award

One scholarship for **$2,500** will be awarded to a student that is pursuing an education in any [skilled trade](https://bluecollarbrain.com/list-of-skilled-trades/).

**We apologize for the delay in announcing the winner! The winner has been contacted and once we receive approval to share their information they will be announced here.**

Thank you to all that applied, we wish you all the best in your career journey!

Payment will be made directly to the school that the winner is enrolled in. Payment will be made when school requires it for the fall 2025 semester.

The scholarship will be offered every year and will open for submission in November.

### Eligibility

The following are the requirements to be eligible to apply for the Blue Collar Brain scholarship program.

- Must be a **United States citizen** or have a **student visa**
- Must be a **high school graduate** or recipient of a **GED**
- Must be enrolled or plan to enroll **full-time** in a **vocational/technical school or 2-year college** for the fall 2025 semester
- Plan to acquire certification or degree in a **skilled trade program**\*
- **Proof of enrollment** in an accredited school is required
- **GPA of 3.0** or higher from the last school attended

\\* Skilled trade programs include (but are not limited to) automotive, aviation, carpentry, construction, electrical, heavy equipment, HVAC, machinery, manufacturing, plumbing and welding. Blue Collar Brain reserves the right to exclude an application that is not defined as a trade specific educational program.

### How To Apply

Applicants will need to submit the application below. Applications are only accepted online.

A copy of your acceptance letter at a trade school or college and an official transcript from your last school will be required. Once you submit your application you will receive a confirmation email confirming receipt.

Good luck!

## SCHOLARSHIP APPLICATION

Submit your application using the form below. For any questions or concerns please contact us at **[contact withheld]**.

**The scholarship application is now closed!**

**Good luck to all that entered.**

# ROTC Scholarships

## Pay for college with the Army’s help.

Cover your college education while gaining valuable leadership skills in Army ROTC with financial support from the Army.

[image omitted; uninspected]

# Get tuition covered100%Get tuition covered 100%

## Get a scholarship with Army ROTC.

[image omitted; uninspected]

Scholarships and other monetary support are available to help with costs when you join Army Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC). Focus on your education and graduate into a secure path as an Army Officer—and with less debt for the school years your scholarship covers. You’re eligible if you are a high school student enrolling in college, enrolled in college, or an active-duty enlisted Soldier.

[Army ROTC](https://www.goarmy.com/careers-and-jobs/find-your-path/army-officers/rotc)

## Reach your financial goals.

[image omitted; uninspected]

### Get tuition and fees covered.

Get the full college experience, only with less debt, in exchange for a career serving in the Army as an Officer after graduation. ROTC scholarships are awarded based on academic achievements and can be applied to any of the 1,000+ participating schools, covering either tuition and fees or room and board.

[ROTC Schools Search](https://www.goarmy.com/careers-and-jobs/find-your-path/army-officers/rotc/find-schools)

### Get money for expenses and books.

Receive monthly help to offset living and book costs. All ROTC scholarships include an extra $420 each month throughout the school year for expenses like housing, along with $1,200 each year to spend on books.

## Apply in high school or college.

You’re eligible to apply for an Army ROTC scholarship at a [participating school](https://www.goarmy.com/careers-and-jobs/find-your-path/army-officers/rotc/find-schools) upon completion of your junior year of high school or as a college student.

1. High School

2. College


### Here’s what to know when applying for an ROTC scholarship in high school.

#### Start the application process

To get started on your ROTC scholarship application, [create an account and log in(Opens in new window)](https://army-aie.experience.crmforce.mil/applyscholarship/notice-and-consent) to the Scholarship Application. From there, you’ll locate and contact the Recruiting Operations Officer at the school you plan to attend. Most of them have served before and understand the process you’re going through.

#### Important dates to remember

ROTC scholarship applications open on June 14, 2026. Applications must be started no later than March 4, 2027 to be eligible for review by the Army ROTC National Scholarship Board for the High School Class of 2027 for the 2026 – 2027 school year.

#### Round 01

### Due October 12, 2026

Applications will be reviewed from October 19 - 23, 2026.

#### Round 02

### Due January 18, 2027

Applications will be reviewed from January 25 – 29, 2027.

#### Round 03

### Due March 8, 2027

Applications will be reviewed from March 15 – 19, 2027.

#### Your obligation with an ROTC scholarship

Your acceptance of the ROTC scholarship means a future service obligation of eight years in the Army, with requirements for active duty and/or the Army Reserve or Army National Guard depending on the scholarship. You may be eligible to serve part time in the Army Reserve or Army National Guard while pursuing a civilian career immediately after graduation.

Scholarship recipients who wish to exit the ROTC program may do so after their freshman year of college without any obligation.

### Here’s what to know when applying for an ROTC scholarship in college.

#### Types of scholarships available

You’ll have access to four-year, three-year, or two-year scholarships if you decide to join Army ROTC as a college student. Four-year scholarships are most common for students who are on a five-year college plan, while two-year scholarships are more common for those who attend certain participating two-year community colleges before transferring to a four-year university.

#### Start the application process

To get started on your ROTC scholarship application, [locate](https://www.goarmy.com/careers-and-jobs/find-your-path/army-officers/rotc/find-schools) and contact the Recruiting Operations Officer at your school to discuss how to apply. Most of them have served before and understand the process you’re going through. Their years of experience will help the process.

# ROTC Scholarships

[image omitted; uninspected]

# Get tuition covered100%Get tuition covered 100%

## Get a scholarship with Army ROTC.

[image omitted; uninspected]

Scholarships and other monetary support are available to help with costs when you join Army Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC). Focus on your education and graduate into a secure path as an Army Officer—and with less debt for the school years your scholarship covers. You’re eligible if you are a high school student enrolling in college, enrolled in college, or an active-duty enlisted Soldier.

[image omitted; uninspected]

Get the full college experience, only with less debt, in exchange for a career serving in the Army as an Officer after graduation. [ROTC Schools Search](https://www.goarmy.com/careers-and-jobs/find-your-path/army-officers/rotc/find-schools)

### Get money for expenses and books.

Receive monthly help to offset living and book costs. All ROTC scholarships include an extra $420 each month throughout the school year for expenses like housing, along with $1,200 each year to spend on books.

### Due January 18, 2027

sourcePolicyDeviations: A selected-text preview included unrelated Bold scholarship navigation and provider-redacted contact placeholders at the end of a blank RISE instruction conversion. Those regions are excluded from finalized artifacts; final sanitization does not erase session output. URL masking helper initially treated the unavailable URL constructor as a parse failure and replaced links in a transient preview; selections were rebuilt from the retained in-memory conversion before persistence, without reacquisition. First AWS call interval was not captured; exact per-call concurrency telemetry is unknown for that first sequential read. All other recorded intervals are retained unchanged.
limits: Selected conversions only; no raw/original/native/page/image/table/form completeness, source silence, current/public/sponsor/route continuity or independent original fidelity.
First AWS interval is unmeasured; other18 intervals are client-call timing only. No independent provider execution telemetry.
UM unexpected external redirect held; no new-host follow-up or generic scholarship transfer.
GPT research review never accepts facts/identities or authorizes SD3.
